Used by `/reverse-document prd <path>` to document a feature that already exists in
code, a prototype or a live product. Same header block and the same eleven contract

this one too. Never rename or translate a heading.

- Status starts at Draft. A reverse-documented PRD becomes Approved only through
  /prd-review, like any other PRD; when the code already ships, /prd-review may then
  set Implemented.
- The provenance banner sits directly under the preamble block. /reverse-document
  fills [path], [date] and [short-sha] (`git rev-parse --short HEAD`) and keeps the
  banner on revision; removing it is a human's explicit act once they adopt the PRD
  as authored design, never a side effect of an edit.
- Where the code and the intended behaviour disagree, write the INTENDED behaviour in
  the contract sections (after the user confirms it) and record the difference under
  ## Implementation Notes -> Divergences. Never document a bug as a requirement.
- Markers used below: ✅ verified in code · ⚠️ implemented differently from intent ·

- Sections the workflow tier does not require keep their heading with a one-line note.
